chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, raising it (as a mursal report) to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Whoever recites the Quran in the mushaf (written copy) will be given benefit in his eyesight, and the punishment will be lightened from his parents, even if they were disbelievers.'

key_terms.خُفِّفَ: To have the punishment lightened; refers to reduction of punishment in the afterlife
key_terms.مُتِّعَ بِبَصَرِهِ: To be given benefit/pleasure in one's eyesight; traditionally understood as preserving or strengthening vision
key_terms.مُصْحَف: The physical written copy of the Quran; distinct from recitation from memory

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reading the Quran from a physical mushaf according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that reading the Quran from a physical written copy (mushaf) carries a distinct spiritual benefit: the reader's eyesight is preserved and strengthened. Remarkably, the narration extends the reward to the reader's parents — even if they died as disbelievers — indicating a form of intercession that transcends religious boundaries. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition's emphasis on the extraordinary merit of Quranic recitation and its capacity to benefit both the living and the deceased.
